words.ex: Kamola and her sister look very alike, but in character they are completely different: one is loud and the other is very quiet.
Jasur is a very positive person: even when his team is losing 3-0 at half-time, he says they can still win.
My neighbour is such a negative person: whatever idea you tell him, he answers, 'That will never work.'
If Sardor says he'll come at nine, he comes at nine; he's completely reliable.
Don't give Bekzod an important job; he's unreliable and often forgets what he promised.
After a month at the speaking club, Nilufar felt confident enough to give a talk in English in front of the whole school.
My little cousin is very shy: when guests come to our house, she hides behind her mother.
Dilshod is very hard-working: he studies until late every night and still helps in his father's shop at weekends.
My brother is so lazy that he asks me to pass him the TV remote when it's just a metre away from him.
Our physics teacher has a great sense of humour; her jokes make even Newton's laws fun.
Our headteacher is a very serious man; I've never seen him laugh, even at the New Year concert.
You have to be patient with a small child who is learning to tie his shoes; it can take ten minutes.
My dad gets very impatient in traffic jams: after two minutes he starts pressing the horn.
Our neighbour is very generous: every autumn he gives a big box of grapes from his vineyard to each family in our street.
My uncle is quite mean with money: he never buys anyone a present, even on their birthday.
When the shop assistant gave him too much change, Sherzod was honest and gave the money back.
The online seller was dishonest: he told us the phone was new, but he knew it was old and broken.
Laylo is so clever that she learned to solve a Rubik's cube in just one evening.
Only a stupid driver looks at his phone while he's driving at a hundred kilometres an hour.
Even when the plane shook in the storm, the pilot's voice stayed calm and relaxed.
Before my first piano concert I was so nervous that my hands were shaking and I couldn't eat anything.
It was so kind of you to feed my cat and water my flowers while I was away in Samarkand.
The traders at the Siab Bazaar in Samarkand were really friendly: they smiled and chatted with us for ages.
It's sensible to charge your phone fully before a long hike, in case you get lost.
My friends laughed at the silly hat with big rabbit ears that I wore to the party.
I told Aziza my secret because I know I can trust her; she never tells anyone.
Our art teacher is very creative: she made a beautiful lamp from old plastic bottles.
Bobur is a talented young musician; he started playing the dutar at six and has already won two competitions.
I wish I could draw like my sister; my pictures always look as if a five-year-old made them.
My sister has a real talent for languages: she learned Turkish just by watching TV series.
Madina is an intelligent girl: she understands new maths topics faster than anyone in her class.
Kids, say thank you to the nice lady who found your ball in her garden.
The hotel receptionist was very pleasant to us: she smiled, chatted about the weather and wished us a good trip.
It was unkind of the older boys to laugh at Otabek when he fell off his bike.
The guard at the gate was unfriendly: he didn't smile or say hello, and just pointed at the sign.
The new manager was so unpleasant to the staff that three people left the company in his first month.
Before Nigora met her new boss, she asked a colleague, 'What's he like?'
